purpose: Close Raiden/J2M as a full land-base interceptor system: production median, variant split, altitude envelope, armament, base readiness, radar/plot/radio-vector integration, attack-cycle limits and target-specific implications. This is a working overlay on TECH-AIR-J2M-FIELDING-1942-43-001; it does not change TECH_INDEX_v009 authority.

historical_sanity_anchors.subject: J2M2/J2M3
historical_sanity_anchors.use: Historical published figures around 596 km/h near 5.45 km and roughly 5:38-5:40 to 6 km are used only to prevent a Branch production median from exceeding plausible airframe/engine physics.

historical_sanity_anchors.subject: J2M3/J2M3a armament
historical_sanity_anchors.use: Historical J2M3 mixed Type 99 Model 1/2 cannon and J2M3a four Model 2 cannon constrain how quickly the Branch can claim ballistic unification.

historical_sanity_anchors.subject: J2M4/J2M5
historical_sanity_anchors.use: Historical turbo-supercharged J2M4 remained troublesome; mechanically supercharged J2M5 demonstrates that high-altitude improvement can exist without granting a mature turbo fleet.

national_inventory_working_1944_01_28.note: Extrapolated from accepted Aug-1943 fielding and 1943H2 30-40/month center. These are January WORKING inventory bands, not a rewrite of the 1943-10 authority ledger.
national_inventory_working_1944_01_28.warning: Do not compare national serviceable inventory with one theater's immediately launchable count. Allocation, base quality and alert posture are separate.

standard_production_raiden.role: 3-8 km short-duration base interception; strongest in roughly 3-6 km band; not a fighter-sweep or long-range escort aircraft.
standard_production_raiden.engine: Kasei 20/23-class Branch production line, about 1,800-1,850 hp class; Branch benefit is cooling/vibration/tolerance median rather than magical rated-power increase.
standard_production_raiden.ceiling_guard: Service ceiling is not practical interception ceiling. At 9-10 km the standard aircraft has little sustained closure margin and depends on early warning/front-quarter geometry.

altitude_bands.assessment: strong acceleration/climb; excellent for low/medium raid interception but vulnerable to escort energy tactics
best overall interception band; useful closure margin against B-24-class bombers when vectoring is timely
still useful, but climb/closure margin declines; attack planning becomes warning-time dependent
marginal sustained chase; useful mainly if already climbing/on altitude or given early front-quarter vector
poor sustained B-29-class chase; one front-quarter pass may be possible with long warning, but do not model parity

high_altitude_mechanical_supercharge_sub.role: limited high-altitude interception subset from the domestic high-altitude Kasei line; a Branch variant family, not a claim that every aircraft is an exact historical J2M5 copy.
high_altitude_mechanical_supercharge_sub.development_clock: ground/high-altitude work 1942; flight integration late-1942 through 1943; limited practical use 1943H2; standardization begins 1944.
high_altitude_mechanical_supercharge_sub.inventory_guard: All figures are subsets of national Raiden totals above, never additive.
high_altitude_mechanical_supercharge_sub.practical_intercept_band: useful into roughly 8.5-9.3 km with adequate warning; 10 km remains marginal, especially for repeat attacks
high_altitude_mechanical_supercharge_sub.allocation_priority: Truk/Palau/home-defense and other strategic A-grade bases before remote outer-island sprinkling.

exhaust_turbo_experimental.role: high-altitude technology test; not counted in operational squadrons
exhaust_turbo_experimental.guard: Do not use turbo-supercharged Raiden performance in 1943 or Jan-1944 combat. Historical J2M4 experience is a caution that rated-altitude gain does not equal service maturity.

armament_state_1944_01_28.frontline_unified_four_Type99_Model2_equ: 35-50% of total frontline Raiden; subset of four-cannon aircraft
armament_state_1944_01_28.mixed_four_cannon_note: A substantial four-cannon population still mixes Model 1/Model 2 ballistic characteristics. Branch testing and production control accelerate convergence but do not erase existing airframes.
armament_state_1944_01_28.bomber_attack_doctrine: Prefer short front-quarter/beam or high-side attacks, using heavy 20-mm volume and minimizing time inside bomber defensive fire; do not center long tail chases.

high_alert_staging_for_18_to_30_aircraft.twenty_to_thirty_minute: remaining serviceable aircraft, subject to maintenance and runway state

control_chain: base plot cell correlation with weather and raid direction
scramble decision and layered altitude assignment
radio vector to coarse intercept box
rejoin / landing / refuel / second alert cycle
base_readiness_and_c2.capability_guard: This is improved Japanese base fighter direction, not US-style continuous precision GCI/CIC. Radar may buy minutes and a coarse vector; visual acquisition still matters and degraded communications can break the loop.

warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.standard_raiden: one late/intermediate-altitude opportunity versus a B-24-type raid if geometry is favorable
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.high_alt_subset: usually too little time for a useful 8-9 km setup
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.B29_note: ground-scramble standard aircraft normally cannot establish a good high-altitude B-29 intercept

warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.standard_raiden: solid 5-7 km interception setup; one attack and possible partial rejoin
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.high_alt_subset: can reach roughly 7.5-8.5 km depending on launch altitude/weather

warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.standard_raiden: can be positioned around 7-8 km for front-quarter/beam interception
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.high_alt_subset: can reach about 8.5-9 km and becomes the real B-29-relevant core
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.B29_note: one good pass becomes plausible; sustained chase does not

warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.standard_raiden: layered setup and a second pass may be possible against predictable medium-altitude raids
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.high_alt_subset: best chance for pre-positioned high-altitude interception
warning_to_intercept_working_matrix.B29_note: repeat attack still constrained by closure, oxygen, engine power, defensive fire and raid track

target_specific_implications.B24_class: At typical 5-7.5 km approach, standard Raiden has meaningful speed/climb margin. Radar-assisted A-grade bases can make it a serious interceptor, but bomber formation fire and escort prevent easy kill assumptions.
target_specific_implications.B29_class: Standard Raiden cannot be converted wholesale into an effective 8.5-10 km B-29 interceptor. Early warning can create a first pass; the limited high-altitude Kasei subset is the relevant core. Future inventories must split variants before computing B-29 losses.
target_specific_implications.F6F_F4U_class: Raiden is dangerous as an energy-rich base-defense interceptor but remains a poor abstraction as a long fighter-sweep duelist. US carrier radar/CIC/fighter direction retains a major system advantage.

marshall_1944_01_28_composition_overlay.accounting: These aircraft are a subset of the already-closed 72 serviceable fighter/local-cover slots in MARSHALL_AIR_OOB; they do not raise theater totals.
marshall_1944_01_28_composition_overlay.unit_identity_guard: Treat as base-defense detachments/allocations until a named kokutai transfer trace is closed; do not rewrite historical unit identity merely to fit aircraft type.

downstream_guards: The 4/30 working figure 'Raiden frontline ready 260-300' is an inventory/readiness figure, not 260-300 B-29-effective high-altitude interceptors.
Do not add A-grade base warning gains to carrier CAP as though the same fixed plot/radar chain exists at sea.
If radar/plot/radio is suppressed, the aircraft retains platform performance but loses much of the system-level exchange benefit.
Do not retroactively change GALVANIC fighter losses: the post-battle procedural learning starts after the battle.
